globalAssertions: Durable continuity is decided only from typed identities and explicit old-target authority.
Rejected operations preserve the complete pre-operation registry, attachment, DAG, certificate-payload and serialized spatial graph.
Invalid current geometry preserves identity and publishes no stale payload.
Every successful copy uses a complete deterministic remap, except an explicitly declared same-construction external-reference policy.
Migration never searches by label, coordinates, proximity, construction order, XML position, output ordinal, layer, view state or Java reference equality.
GeoCeDG Classic is the fork Classic process using the same shared kernel; it is not external upstream GeoGebra.
External upstream support is characterized as unsupported-open and no lossy compatibility conversion is added.

cases.title: Add second defining binding
cases.expected: Owner identities persist, the binding is fresh, declared revisions advance and UNDERDETERMINED becomes VALID.

cases.title: Remove defining binding
cases.expected: The exact binding retires, owner identities persist and VALID becomes UNDERDETERMINED with no payload.

cases.title: Re-role binding and recover
cases.expected: DEFINING to AUXILIARY or PRESENTATION and back is atomic, revisioned and deterministically recoverable.

cases.title: Reject mixed derived authority
cases.expected: A forbidden DERIVED or mixed-authority proposal leaves graph, certificate and XML state unchanged.

cases.title: Mutate frame, map and relation membership
cases.expected: Reciprocal membership, fresh or retired child identities and exact declared revision deltas remain coherent.

cases.title: Map value invalidation and recovery
cases.expected: Only durable dependents update through the normal DAG; invalidity withdraws payload and recovery is current.

cases.title: Hinge support compatible redefine
cases.expected: The support identity persists, relation/system/point recompute and invalid-to-valid recovery is deterministic.

cases.title: Delete dependency and recreate same appearance
cases.expected: The recreated geo has fresh identity and no broken reference rebinds by label or coordinates.

cases.title: True projection-system replacement
cases.expected: Every affected old dependent is explicitly retired, the replacement closure is fresh and complete, existing geo attachments are preserved, and no identity is inferred or rebound.

cases.title: Zero through three defining bindings
cases.expected: UNDEFINED, UNDERDETERMINED, VALID, INCONSISTENT and DEGENERATE transitions are explicit and never retain stale payload.

cases.title: Same-document complete closure
cases.expected: Every owned typed identity is fresh-remapped and immediate copy provenance is exact.

cases.title: Cross-document complete closure
cases.expected: All live references resolve inside the destination closure and none point to the source construction.

cases.title: Declared same-construction external references
cases.expected: Only explicitly allow-listed active system or map identities remain shared.

cases.title: Undeclared same-document partial closure
cases.expected: The whole copy rejects atomically with no dangling record.

cases.title: Cross-document external reference
cases.expected: A partial or live external cross-construction reference rejects atomically.

cases.title: Recursive relation closure
cases.expected: Relation endpoints, auxiliary maps/frames and support geos are included and remapped.

cases.title: Repeated paste and macro
cases.expected: Each instance is disjoint, internally coherent and deterministic for the same source closure.

cases.title: Copy, re-role, undo, redo and delete
cases.expected: Every step has an exact identity graph and the construction registry remains bounded.

cases.title: Explicit semantic no-op
cases.expected: RETAIN preserves all identities and advances neither definition nor topology revision.

cases.title: Same-object or null host no-op
cases.expected: The host route cannot fabricate a lifecycle change.

cases.title: Independent undefined numeric route
cases.expected: Explicit compatible authority is preserved and rollback remains pre-operation exact.

cases.title: In-place set route
cases.expected: Compatible change retains identity and advances definition exactly once.

cases.title: Soft redefine route
cases.expected: Compatible change has the same lifecycle result as every other admitted host route.

cases.title: No-child new-instance route
cases.expected: The replacement instance receives the explicit target identity without Java-instance inference.

cases.title: Circular numeric route
cases.expected: Participating identity is either explicitly retained under the provider contract or atomically rejected.

cases.title: Circular point, vector and boolean route
cases.expected: Every subroute obeys the same explicit-target and rollback policy.

cases.title: Collected retained batch route
cases.expected: The whole mapped group commits or rolls back as one transaction.

cases.title: Full XML rebuild route
cases.expected: The serialization overlay restores the decided identities and exact revisions without XML-order authority.

cases.title: AlgebraProcessor explicit target
cases.expected: Target authority captured before parsing controls continuity.

cases.title: ParametricProcessor explicit target
cases.expected: The provider predicate, not expression or label equality, controls continuity.

cases.title: AlgoDispatcher path and region routes
cases.expected: Pre-operation authority covers attach and detach replacement paths and failures restore the original graph.

cases.title: EuclidianController3D move-release route
cases.expected: Context and rollback snapshot precede helper-point creation; failure restores pre-operation state.

cases.title: Label and XML-discovered no-authority routes
cases.expected: Participating targets reject; label or bounding-box replacement cannot retain identity.

cases.title: GeoCasCell direct route
cases.expected: Participating targets remain unsupported and reject atomically.

cases.title: PolygonFactory guarded route
cases.expected: Participating rewrites remain conservatively rejected.

cases.title: Compatible route equivalence
cases.expected: Every admitted route yields the same identity, definition plus one, unchanged topology and current certificate.

cases.title: Incompatible redefine
cases.expected: Type, schema, family, authority or role incompatibility yields atomic REJECT.

cases.title: Explicit true replacement
cases.expected: FRESH identities replace the old meaning and undo restores the exact old snapshot.

cases.title: Missing explicit target context
cases.expected: Continuity is never retained without the captured target.

cases.title: Label-only apparent compatibility
cases.expected: Same label, type, coordinates or construction position never grants RETAIN.

cases.title: Stale target context
cases.expected: A superseded transaction cannot overwrite a newer registry or runtime publication.

cases.title: Provider-owned stable-role output group
cases.expected: Exact-cardinality outputs retain by unique persisted role even when the candidate array is reordered.

cases.title: Ambiguous or cardinality-changing output group
cases.expected: Missing or duplicate roles, partial siblings, ordinal-only mapping or changed cardinality rejects and rolls back.

cases.title: Repeated save and reopen
cases.expected: Two cycles preserve exact graph, revisions and normalized spatial XML.

cases.title: Repeated undo and redo
cases.expected: Binding mutation, re-role and delete snapshots restore exact identities.

cases.title: Redefine, reopen, replacement and undo
cases.expected: Compatible continuity and later true replacement remain distinguishable and reversible.

cases.title: Persist invalid state and recover
cases.expected: Invalid identities reopen without payload and exact typed repair deterministically recovers them.

cases.title: Injected mutation or load failure
cases.expected: Interrupted resolution restores the complete registry, DAG, payload and XML entry snapshot.

cases.title: Legacy file without spatial section
cases.expected: The file remains valid and all ordinary geos remain unassociated.

cases.title: Version-one inert records
cases.expected: They remain inert and do not imply version-two POINT semantics.

cases.title: Shuffled version-two forward closure
cases.expected: Two-stage load resolves deterministically independent of XML order.

cases.title: Missing binding or map reference
cases.expected: The graph is explicitly broken or the load rejects according to the native atomic policy; it is never repaired.

cases.title: Missing relation support or endpoint
cases.expected: The exact missing durable identity is diagnosed and no geometry is inferred.

cases.title: Duplicate native durable identity
cases.expected: Native load rejects atomically and never remaps.

cases.title: Malformed kind, role, family or schema
cases.expected: Strict parsing or prospective validation rejects before publication.

cases.title: Unknown attribute or future version
cases.expected: Outer and record future versions fail truthfully with no opaque or lossy fallback.

cases.title: Native collision versus import collision
cases.expected: Native load rejects while explicit import remaps the complete closure.

cases.title: Deterministic normalized rewrite
cases.expected: Repeated reopen produces identical canonical record order and identity graph.

cases.title: Complete explicit POINT association
cases.expected: Caller-selected GeoElements plus a complete typed plan atomically allocate fresh identities and explicit-association provenance.

cases.title: No request under adversarial appearance
cases.expected: Coincident geometry, suggestive labels, layers and order permutations create zero associations.

cases.title: Incomplete or ambiguous plan
cases.expected: The service rejects without scanning or guessing.

cases.title: Stale, foreign or deleted target
cases.expected: The explicit plan rejects atomically before identity allocation becomes live.

cases.title: Repeated explicit plan
cases.expected: The second application is an explicit already-associated no-op or typed rejection and never duplicates the graph.

cases.title: Migrate, copy, disable feature and reopen
cases.expected: The associated graph persists exactly; disabling creation never strips native records.

cases.title: GeoCeDG native round trip
cases.expected: AppConfigGeoCeDG loads, recomputes, saves and reopens the native POINT model exactly.

cases.title: Fork Classic diagnostic round trip
cases.expected: AppConfigDefault uses the same shared kernel and preserves the exact native identity graph and certificates.

cases.title: Classic creation boundary
cases.expected: No public spatial creation workflow is exposed while native records remain readable and writable.

cases.title: External upstream unsupported-open boundary
cases.expected: The target is classified unsupported and converter or downgrade invocation count remains zero.

cases.title: Foreign resave without spatial section
cases.expected: Ordinary geometry loads as legacy and remains unassociated; no label/list/coordinate repair occurs.

cases.title: Authority hard-zero counters
cases.expected: Inference, downgrade, stale-publication, hidden-graph and view-state counters remain zero while transaction counters match outcomes.

cases.title: Forbidden-scope audit
cases.expected: No G9B/G9C/G9U, GUI, command, DXF, Locus, Python, general genealogy or new primitive implementation is present.

cases.title: Hostile-sequence boundedness
cases.expected: The final registry is bounded, reciprocal, free of dangling references and contains no tracked generated bundle.
